questions.question: What makes a strong thesis statement?
options: It is specific, debatable and supportable
It is a general fact everyone agrees on
It is a question
It lists every point in the essay
questions.explanation: A strong thesis is specific, debatable and supportable, usually placed at the end of the introduction.

questions.question: In a PEEL paragraph, which part is described as the most important?
options: The Explanation — analysing the significance of the evidence
The Point
The Evidence
The Link
questions.explanation: The explanation is where you analyse why the evidence matters — without it, evidence is just a quotation.

questions.question: How should you handle counter-arguments in argumentative writing?
options: Acknowledge them, concede valid points, then rebut with stronger reasoning
Ignore them completely
Agree with all of them
Mock the people who hold them
questions.explanation: Acknowledging and rebutting counter-arguments shows careful thinking and strengthens your own position.

questions.question: Where is the thesis statement usually placed?
options: At the end of the introduction
In the title
In the middle of a body paragraph
Only in the conclusion
questions.explanation: The introduction hooks the reader, provides context and builds to the thesis at its end.

questions.question: What should a strong conclusion do?
options: Restate the thesis in new words, synthesize main points and point to broader implications
Introduce brand new arguments
Repeat the introduction word for word
Apologise for possible errors
questions.explanation: A conclusion restates the thesis freshly, synthesizes the argument and may end with broader implications or a call to action.
